title: Find the bug in a second_largest function
prompt:
This function is supposed to return the second largest number in a list but crashes when the list has duplicates of the largest value.

def second_largest(nums):
    unique = sorted(set(nums))
    return unique[-2]

Identify the bug and explain the fix.

metadata.notes: Bug: if all values are identical (e.g. [5, 5, 5]), `unique` has only 1 element and unique[-2] raises IndexError. Fix should handle the case where fewer than 2 distinct values exist. Graded manually.
metadata.known_ambiguity: What the fixed function SHOULD return for input like [5,5,5] is itself underspecified (return 5 again? raise a clear error? return None?) - flagged as a known spec gap, same class of issue as is_anagram had before its prompt was fixed. Not resolved here; grade generously for any reasonable, explicitly-stated choice.
metadata.deterministic_grading_attempted_and_reje: 2026-09-23 (V2.6 Phase 1): tried converting this to sandboxed test-based grading and verified the result before using it, per the process used for the other 7 debugging tasks. The only test case that actually distinguishes the buggy implementation from a fixed one is the all-duplicate case (e.g. [5,5,5]) that crashes the original - but that is exactly the input whose correct return value is the unresolved ambiguity above. Testing every OTHER input (any list with >=2 distinct values) passes against the ORIGINAL BUGGY CODE UNCHANGED, since it never crashes on those. Verified directly: sorted([5,3,8,1]) has 4 distinct values, sorted([10,10,20]) has 2 - buggy code returns the correct second-largest for both without modification. So this task cannot be made deterministically gradable without either (a) picking one canonical answer for the ambiguous case, which would be resolving ground truth merely to make grading convenient (explicitly not done), or (b) adding a new test type that checks 'does not raise an exception' without asserting a specific return value, which the sandbox grader does not support yet. Staying manual.
